topics.title: Building SyteLine forms
topics.subtitle: For the people who build and change Enflite forms in SyteLine
topics.summary: How Enflite builds SyteLine forms: when to add UET fields and when to build a new table, IDO and form, and how to pick column data types.

blocks.text: These pages are for the people who build Enflite forms, not for the people who fill them in. They collect what we have learned building **eCMRs**, **Service Orders** and **Incidents**.

head: Situation
Approach
Example
rows: You need a few more fields on a form Infor already has
Add **UET** fields to Infor's form, and import the changed form through **FormSync**
No existing form fits, and the new form doesn't have to work with other forms or their event handlers
Build a **new table + new IDO + new form**

blocks.text: Never change Infor's own tables, IDOs or forms. Build everything on **TRN** first; production repeats the same steps from the same files.

topics.title: Create a custom table and IDO
topics.subtitle: The table, the IDO on top of it, then the form
topics.summary: Create a ue_ table in Application Studio, add its columns, build an IDO on it and check it in, then import the form through FormSync.

blocks.text: Use this when no existing form fits (see [Building SyteLine forms](/syteline/build)). The order matters: **table**, then **IDO**, then **form**. The form binds every field to an IDO property by name, and FormSync can only import forms: it can't create a table or an IDO.

items: Where
**Application Studio**, project `ue_ENF`
Environment
TRN first, then production
Worked example
`ue_ecmrs` (eCMRs), live on TRN
Sources

Recorded walkthrough of a new `ue_` table (2026); the eCMRs build ([Implementation Plan](https://github.com/Enflite/eCMRs/blob/main/docs/Implementation-Plan.md), [troubleshooting](https://github.com/Enflite/eCMRs/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md))
Write down every field the form needs, from the team's source (their spreadsheet or mockup): name, what it holds, how long it can be, and whether it can be empty.
Pick the table name: `ue_<name>`, lower case (e.g. `ue_ecmrs`). `ue_` marks a table we created; everything else is Infor's.
Check the name isn't used yet: no table, IDO or form by that name in the environment.
In **Application Studio**, open **SQL Tables** and click **New**.

Enter the table name (`ue_<name>`) and **Save**. Application Studio adds seven standard columns itself: `CreatedBy`, `UpdatedBy`, `CreateDate`, `RecordDate`, `RowPointer`, `NoteExistsFlag` and `InWorkflow`. Don't add them again.
Open the table's **Columns** and add one row per field. Name each column in `snake_case` (`computer_name`, `cmr_num`).
For each column choose its **Data Type**: an existing SyteLine type when one fits, else a plain type with a length. See [Choosing a column's data type](/syteline/build/data-types).

Set **Nullable**. Leave it ticked when the field may be empty. Clear it only for fields every record must have (the key, and fields like a serial number): SyteLine then refuses to save a record without them.
Make the key column the table's **Primary Key** (on eCMRs: `cmr_num`). Each record's key must be different, and the form or the user has to fill it in before saving.
**Save**.
Open **IDOs** and start a new IDO (the **IDO wizard**). Project `ue_ENF`.
Name the IDO the same as the table (`ue_<name>`), set the **Primary Base Table** to your table and give it a short **table alias** (eCMRs uses `ec`).
Add one **IDO Property** per column: **Bind To** the column, and name the property in `PascalCase` (`cmr_num` → `CmrNum`). The form binds to the property name (`object.CmrNum`), not the column.
Set each property's **Data Type** (`String`, `Date`, `Decimal`...) and give it the **same Length as its column**.
Leave **Property Class** and **Column Data Type** blank on your own properties.
On the key property, mark the key (**Pseudo Key** 1 on eCMRs).
Set what the form needs: an **Inline List** for fixed drop-down values, and clear **Read Only Record** on fields the form fills in itself.

**Check In** the IDO (IDOs tab → your IDO → **Check In**). Changes to IDO properties don't take effect until you do. The message “Source control integration is currently disabled” is harmless: click **OK**.
Export the **SQL Columns** and **IDO Properties** grids to Excel.
Check every column is there with the right type, and every IDO property's length equals its column's.
Keep the exports in the project repo (`docs/reference/`). They are the checklist for building production, and the exact format any import file has to match.
Build the form XML from the project's build script (never by hand, and never as a Design Mode change).
Import it through **FormSync** at **Site** scope.
Test: **New**, fill in, **Save**, reopen. Then make the form available to users (menu, form security).

Instead of typing every row, columns and properties can be imported from CSV files on the **SQL Columns** and **IDO Properties** grids (eCMRs did this for production). The file must match a fresh export of the same grid exactly (header, column count, quoting). A mismatch fails silently rather than with an error.

In an SQL Columns import, **Data Type** must be a real type (`nvarchar`, `char`, `datetime`, `decimal`, or a named type like `UsernameType`). The word `String` is refused: *“String is not a valid Data Type.”*

If an IDO property is longer than its column, saving fails with *“String or binary data would be truncated in table ...”*. If it's shorter than the value, the message is *“Data length for <field> (n) is greater than effective length (m)”*.

Don't generate the key with `AUTONUMBER` in the IDO's **Default Value**: on eCMRs it repeated numbers and saves failed with `PK_ue_ecmrs`. eCMRs sets the key from a form script on **New** instead (`CMR-YYMMDD-HHMMSS`).
A table you create in **SQL Tables** is a real database table. No separate database step is needed.

blocks.text: Not yet confirmed: the recorded walkthrough named its columns `Uf_ComputerName`, `Uf_SerialNumber`... . `Uf_` is our prefix for UET fields; on a table we own, columns are `snake_case` like eCMRs'. The recording also ends at the start of the IDO wizard, so the IDO steps above come from the eCMRs build.

topics.title: Choosing a column's data type
topics.subtitle: Reuse the types SyteLine already has
topics.summary: Use an existing SyteLine data type when one fits (it brings its length and format), how to find the type a standard field uses, and what to use when none fits.

blocks.text: Every column needs a data type. Where SyteLine already has a type for that kind of value (a username, an item, a date), use it: its length and format are already decided, and your field then matches Infor's fields that hold the same thing.

head: Holds
Type
Notes
rows: A long name (e.g. a computer name)
What SyteLine uses for its own `InWorkflow` column
A date, or date and time
Our own text, with no matching type
eCMRs uses `char(255)` for its own text

blocks.text: Find the type a standard field uses
To store the same kind of value as a field on one of Infor's forms (for example the username on **Employees**), look up the type that field uses:

items: Open the form (e.g. **Employees**) in **Design Mode**.
Select the field and read its **Binding**: the IDO property it shows (`object.<Property>`). The form's collection names the IDO.
Open **IDOs**, find that IDO and open its **Properties**.
Select the property and read its **Column Data Type** (e.g. `UsernameType`).
Use that type for your column.

blocks.text: Only look in Design Mode. Don't change the form there: our form changes go through the build script and FormSync.

items: Use `nvarchar` (or `char`) with a length that fits the longest real value, with some room. Short codes and statuses: 60. Notes: 600 or more.
In **SQL Columns**, the **Data Type** must be a real type (`nvarchar`, `char`, `datetime`, `decimal`, or a named type). The word `String` is refused.
The IDO property's **Data Type** is the generic kind (`String`, `Date`, `Decimal`), and its **Length** must equal the column's.

blocks.text: **Nullable** ticked means the field may be left empty. Leave it ticked unless every record must have a value. Cleared, SyteLine won't save a record without it, so clear it only for the key and fields that are always known (e.g. a serial number).

topics.title: Builder glossary
topics.subtitle: SyteLine terms used when building forms
topics.summary: What the SyteLine terms used when building forms mean: IDO, UET, data type, nullable, primary key, FormSync and our naming prefixes.

head: Term
Meaning
rows: Infor CloudSuite Industrial, our ERP. Its web client is built on Infor **Mongoose**.
The training (test) environment. Everything is built and proven here before production.
Where tables and IDOs are created and changed (**SQL Tables**, **IDOs**).
Where the data is stored. A column is one field of every record.
Intelligent Data Object: the layer between a form and its table(s). Forms read and save data only through an IDO.
One field of an IDO, bound to a table column. A form field binds to it as `object.<Property>`.
What a column holds and how long it can be. SyteLine has named types (`UsernameType`, `ItemType`...) that carry a length and format.
The field may be left empty. When cleared, a record can't be saved without it.
The column that identifies each record. No two records can have the same value.
A lookup the database keeps on one or more columns, so searches and joins on them are fast.
A fixed list of values set on an IDO property, used for a drop-down.
An IDO property flag: the property can't be changed. Clear it on fields the form fills in.
Saves IDO changes so they take effect.
User Extended Tables: adds our own fields to Infor's tables without changing them. Used on Service Orders and Incidents.
SyteLine's form designer. We use it to look at a form, never to deliver changes.
Imports a form XML file into SyteLine. We import at **Site** scope, never over Infor's own (Vendor) version.
A table or IDO we created (e.g. `ue_ecmrs`).
Marks anything Enflite created. Without it, it's Infor's.
